variants.name: County Commission and School Board elections
variants.summary: Nonpartisan seats elected by district in the August primary of even years; if no one wins a majority, the top two meet in a runoff on the November general election ballot. New terms start the second Tuesday after the general election.
variants.dayCounting: Offsets are calendar days from the anchor; "29 days before" is offset -29.

milestones.name: Candidate qualifying
milestones.actor: Candidates, filing with the Supervisor of Elections

timing.rule: Noon of the 71st day to noon of the 67th day before the primary.

residentCan.how: Run: file papers and the fee, or petition signatures by the earlier petition deadline.

milestones.influenceWhy: Decides who you can choose from.

milestones.name: Campaign finance reports
milestones.output: Public reports: every other Friday from the 60th day before the primary to the 4th day before the general, plus reports on the 25th and 11th days before each election

timing.rule: Quarterly, then on the pre-election schedule; the filing officer publishes exact dates.

residentCan.how: Read who is funding each candidate on the Supervisor of Elections site.

milestones.influenceWhy: Lets voters weigh who funds a candidate before voting.

milestones.name: Primary election
milestones.output: Winner with a majority, or top two to the runoff

timing.rule: The Tuesday 11 weeks before the general election.

residentCan.how: Vote; nonpartisan races are open to all registered voters.

milestones.influenceWhy: Many seats are decided outright here.

milestones.name: Voter registration closes

timing.rule: 29 days before the election.

residentCan.how: Register or update your address by this date.

milestones.influenceWhy: Miss it and you cannot vote in this election.

milestones.name: Last day to request a mail ballot

timing.rule: 5 p.m. on the 12th day before the election.

residentCan.how: Request a mail ballot by this deadline; it must be received by 7 p.m. on election day (s. 101.67(2), F.S.).

milestones.name: Early voting
milestones.output: Votes cast in person before election day

timing.rule: Required from the 10th to the 3rd day before the election; the Supervisor may add any of the 15th to 11th days and the 2nd day, so the outer limit is the 15th to the 2nd day.

residentCan.how: Vote early at any early voting site in the county.

timing.rule: The first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of even years.

residentCan.how: Vote at your precinct, 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.

timing.rule: Noon on the 4th day after a general election.

residentCan.how: Canvassing board meetings are public.

milestones.name: Recount if the margin is close
milestones.output: Machine recount at 0.5% or less; manual recount of over and under votes at 0.25% or less

timing.rule: After unofficial results; the trailing candidate may waive.

residentCan.how: Canvassing board meetings are public; you may observe.

timing.rule: Noon on the 13th day after a general election.

residentCan.how: Read the certified precinct results.

milestones.name: Election contest window
milestones.output: Contest filed in circuit court, or results stand

timing.rule: Within 10 days after certification.

residentCan.how: A qualified voter may file a contest in circuit court within 10 days of certification.

milestones.name: New terms begin

timing.rule: The second Tuesday after the general election.

residentCan.how: Introduce yourself to the new member's office and name your top issue.

milestones.influenceWhy: New members set staff and priorities in their first weeks.

milestones.name: Campaign accounts closed and final report

timing.rule: Within 90 days after the candidate is elected, eliminated or unopposed.

residentCan.how: Read the final report to see where leftover money went.

milestones.influenceWhy: After the fact, but it shows who funded the winner.

variants.name: City elections
variants.summary: City charters set qualifying, election and runoff dates and when terms begin. State law still sets registration, mail ballot, campaign finance, recount and contest rules.
variants.dayCounting: Offsets are calendar days from the anchor; "29 days before" is offset -29.

milestones.name: Candidate qualifying
milestones.actor: Candidates, filing with the City Clerk

timing.rule: Set by the city charter or code; the city may change it by ordinance.

residentCan.how: Run: file with the City Clerk during the window.

milestones.influenceWhy: Decides who you can choose from.

milestones.name: Campaign finance reports
milestones.output: Public reports filed with the City Clerk on the state schedule

timing.rule: The City Clerk gives each candidate the schedule; cities may not adopt a different one.

residentCan.how: Read the reports on the clerk's site or ask the clerk.

milestones.influenceWhy: Lets voters weigh who funds a candidate before voting.

milestones.name: Voter registration closes

timing.rule: 29 days before the election.

residentCan.how: Register or update your address by this date.

milestones.influenceWhy: Miss it and you cannot vote in this election.

milestones.name: Last day to request a mail ballot

timing.rule: 5 p.m. on the 12th day before the election.

residentCan.how: Request a mail ballot by this deadline; it must be received by 7 p.m. on election day (s. 101.67(2), F.S.).

milestones.name: Early voting
milestones.actor: Supervisor of Elections or the city

timing.rule: When held with a state election: required from the 10th to the 3rd day before, and the Supervisor may add the 15th to 11th and the 2nd day. A city election held alone may offer early voting at its own sites.

residentCan.how: Vote early at any county early voting site when the city election is on a county ballot.

milestones.name: City election
milestones.output: Winner, or a runoff where the charter requires a majority

timing.rule: Set by the city charter.

residentCan.how: Vote, 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.

milestones.name: Recount if the margin is close
milestones.output: Machine recount at 0.5% or less; manual recount of over and under votes at 0.25% or less

timing.rule: After unofficial results; the trailing candidate may waive.

residentCan.how: Canvassing board meetings are public; you may observe.

timing.rule: Set by the city charter or code and the canvassing board.

residentCan.how: Read the certified results.

milestones.name: Election contest window
milestones.output: Contest filed in circuit court, or results stand

timing.rule: Within 10 days after certification.

residentCan.how: A qualified voter may file a contest in circuit court within 10 days of certification.

milestones.name: Runoff election (if needed)

timing.rule: Set by the city charter.

residentCan.how: Vote in the runoff; registration closes 29 days before it.

milestones.influenceWhy: Runoffs often have low turnout, so each vote weighs more.

milestones.name: New terms begin

timing.rule: Set by the city charter.

residentCan.how: Introduce yourself to the new member and name your top issue.

milestones.influenceWhy: New members set priorities in their first weeks.

milestones.name: Campaign accounts closed and final report

timing.rule: Within 90 days after the candidate is elected, eliminated or unopposed.

residentCan.how: Read the final report to see where leftover money went.

milestones.influenceWhy: After the fact, but it shows who funded the winner.
